q: What CBAM figure does an EU buyer need for rails from Bhilai?
title: Bhilai rails: the CBAM figure
short: Rails fall under CN 7302, so they are CBAM goods. The buyer needs embedded emissions per tonne of rail, from the integrated works through the rail mill, verified for the definitive regime. Integrated blast furnace mills sit well above scrap based mills, so measured data matters.
audience: Rail mills in Bhilai and Indian traders supplying rails and track material abroad

ul: Coke, sinter, blast furnace and converter emissions.
Rail mill fuel and process gases.

p: One figure per tonne of rail, with the period and method. Only direct emissions count toward the steel charge; electricity is reported separately.
Most Bhilai rails go to Indian Railways. The figure still matters for any export lot and for Indian buyers asking for Scope 3 data.

senseible: Senseible keeps each site's fuel, power and production records together, so the embedded emissions you send an EU importer trace back to dated documents.
